description: Für die Ertüchtigung der Umleiterstrecke Lübeck – Büchen (Strecke 1121), die im Rahmen der Generalsanierung Lübeck - Hamburg umgesetzt werden soll, müssen diverse Verkehre umgeleitet werden. title: Ireland – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – Invitation to tender for the Provision of a Digital PCR Platform, Associated Reagents and Support for Cancer Molecular Diagnostics Department within St James’s Hospital Dublin
description: The Contracting Authority (CA) seeks to purchase one digital PCR instrument, including all hardware, software and ancillary equipment required for routine operation. The purchase shall include a minimum three-year comprehensive warranty, installation, commissioning and training.The CA intends initially to use the platform for assay development, evaluation and method transfer and wishes to purchase an agreed quantity/value of development reagents and consumables at the commencement of the contract. These reagents shall be available for draw-down by the laboratory as required over the three-year agreement. During the course of the agreement, the CA may elect to develop new assays or migrate selected existing molecular diagnostic assays to dPCR where this provides appropriate clinical, analytical or operational benefit. The extent and timing of such migration will be determined by the CA according to clinical and service requirements and does not represent a commitment to implement any specific assay or purchase any minimum quantity of reagents.

title: Denmark – Home-help services – Udbud af helhedspleje efter ældreloven og hjemmepleje efter serviceloven til borgere i eget hjem
description: Udbuddet omfatter levering af helhedspleje efter ældreloven og levering af hjemmepleje efter serviceloven til hjemmeboende borgere i Rudersdal Kommune. Opgaver omfattet af Sundhedsloven indgår også i udbuddet, ligesom der er en obligatorisk option på levering af almen sygepleje, som forventes integreret i helhedsplejen i takt med ændringer i Sundhedsloven. Der indgås aftale med en leverandører. Ydelserne er omfattet af reglerne om frit valg, og borgerne i Rudersdal Kommune vil således med dette udbud kunne vælge mellem den kommunale leverandør og den private leverandør. Omfanget af de ydelser der skal leveres, afhænger af antallet af visiterede borgere der vælger den private leverandør. Udbuddet omfatter helhedspleje og afløsning efter ældrelovens § 10 og § 16 samt personlig og praktisk hjælp, rehabilitering og afløsning og aflastning efter servicelovens § 83, 83a og §84. Udbuddet omfatter ligeledes delegerede sygeplejeydelser efter sundhedslovens § 138 til modtagere af helhedspleje og hjemmepleje, samt en option på almen sygepleje efter sundhedslovens § 138.

title: Ireland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Multi Operator Framework for Project Managers with Design/Technical Consultants for Educational Accommodation
description: The Project Management Services that are being procured under this competition are for the organising, overseeing and management, procurement and delivery of SEN refurbishing within existing school buildings and/or the provision of modular accommodation for SEN and/or mainstream classroom and ancillary space with associated site works. The services will include both the management and the delivery of the services. The successful Project Management Firm shall receive a brief from the Department of Education and Youth to refurbish existing spaces within a school for a new purpose or to deliver a new accommodation on the grounds of an existing school or a combination of both. The required Project Management service will comprise of three parts A, B and C. Part A will consist of the successful Project management firm and their Multi-Disciplinary Design Team (MDDT) visiting the school to assess the most economically advantageous location to the deliver the brief while identify the capacity of existing services identify risks and preparing an order of magnitude costing. Part B is only applicable to projects where the brief requires refurbishment of existing school spaces by contractors using the “Framework Agreement for Term Maintenance, Refurbishment and Upgrade Construction Works to Educational Facilities” (PW CF-11) which will be referred to as the “Refurbishing Framework” in the remainder of this document. As an Employer led design project the PM and their MDDT will develop the detailed design drawings and supervise the contractor during construction Part C will only be applicable to projects where the project brief requires additional accommodation to be delivered via the Departments of Education and Youth’s “Multi-Operator Framework Agreement for the Provision of MMC Pre-Manufactured Modular 3D Volumetric Educational Accommodation” (PW CF-02) Which will be referred to as the “Modular Framework” in the remainder of this document. As a design build contract the PM’s Multidisciplinary Design Team will become Technical Designers as they develop the preliminary brief design that the contractors will take to complete the detailed design and construct.

title: France – Parts for warships – M26T20025 - Fourniture de matériels électroniques courants pour les forces armées françaises
description: Le présent avis concerne un accord-cadre à commandes en ligne, via un catalogue électronique, portant sur l’approvisionnement de matériels électroniques courants pour les forces armées françaises. Le projet de marché porte sur une offre de fournitures suffisamment étendue pour répondre à la diversité des besoins. Ce projet s’adresse exclusivement à des fabricants ou à des distributeurs de composants électroniques, ayant une gamme de produits développée et accessible directement en ligne (catalogue électronique) et avec paiement par carte-achats. Il concerne essentiellement le matériel d’utilisation courante, non spécialisé, peu coûteux et facile à approvisionner dans des délais très courts inférieurs à 30 jours. Forme du marché : Le présent avis concerne un marché de défense ou de sécurité ayant pour objet « la fourniture de matériels électroniques courants pour les forces armées françaises ». L’accord cadre est à commandes par carte achat 3 sur catalogue électronique, conformément aux dispositions de l’article L. 2325-1 du code de la commande publique et selon les modalités précisées au II.2.2. En application de l’article R. 2362-9 du code de la commande publique, les offres devront comporter un catalogue électronique aux conditions fixées par l’acheteur. Elles peuvent être accompagnées par d’autres documents qui les complètent. La procédure est un appel d’offres restreint avec réduction du délai de réception des candidatures et des offres à 10 jours, conformément aux dispositions de l’article R. 2361-6 du Code de la commande publique. La présente publication concerne uniquement un appel à candidature. Le dossier de consultation sera envoyé ultérieurement et uniquement aux candidats admis à soumissionner. Mots descripteurs : matériels électroniques (articles)

title: H212-- Fire Pump Test and Alarm support
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Annual NFPA 25 Fire Pump Inspection and Performance Testing Hudson Valley VA Health Care System Castle Point Campus Notice Type: Sources Sought / Market Research This is not a solicitation. This notice is issued solely for conducting market research in accordance with FAR Part 10. The Government is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of providing annual fire pump inspection and performance testing services. Responses will be used to determine the availability of capable sources and the appropriate acquisition strategy. Contracting Activity Department of Veterans Affairs Hudson Valley VA Health Care System Place of Performance Hudson Valley VA Medical Center Castle Point Campus 41 Castle Point Road Wappingers Falls, NY 12590 Tentative NAICS and PSC NAICS: 561621, Equipment and Materials Testing Fire Control Equipment PSC: H212, Equipment and Materials Testing: Fire Control Equipment Requirement Description The Department of Veterans Affairs is conducting market research to identify qualified contractors capable of performing annual fire pump testing in accordance with the edition of NFPA 25 applicable to the facility and other applicable VA requirements. This requirement is for annual testing and inspection services only. Repairs, replacement parts, and corrective maintenance resulting from testing are not included in the contemplated contract. The contractor shall provide qualified personnel, testing equipment, labor, supervision, and documentation necessary to perform annual fire pump inspection and performance testing. Services include, but are not limited to: Visual inspection of fire pump, driver, controller, and associated equipment. Verification of pump room conditions and compliance with NFPA 25 requirements. Inspection of suction and discharge piping, valves, gauges, and relief valves. Verification of controller settings, alarms, and power supply. Churn (no-flow) testing. Full-flow performance testing at 100% and 150% rated flow, where water supply permits. Measurement and documentation of suction pressure, discharge pressure, flow, RPM, voltage, amperage, and other required performance data. Verification of pump and controller operation. Verification of supervisory and fire alarm signals affected by testing. Documentation of deficiencies, limitations, and performance results. Restoration of systems to normal operating condition following testing. Deliverables The contractor shall provide, at a minimum: Annual fire pump performance test report. Flow test data sheets and forms. Pump performance curve comparison. Inspection and test documentation. Deficiency report identifying observed impairments and recommended corrective actions. Documentation of any test limitations encountered during performance. Contractor Qualification Requirements Interested vendors should demonstrate: Experience performing annual NFPA 25 fire pump testing. Qualified personnel with documented training and experience. NICET Level II or higher in Inspection and Testing of Water-Based Systems, or equivalent qualifications, if available. Appropriate licensing, certifications, and insurance. Availability of calibrated flow and pressure testing equipment or evidence of measurement accuracy. Ability to coordinate with facility representatives and affected fire alarm monitoring/support personnel. Response Requested Interested firms shall submit the following information: Company name. UEI. CAGE Code. Business size status. Socioeconomic status (e.g., SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, HUBZone, Small Business, Large Business). Primary NAICS code. Capability statement (maximum five pages). Description of experience performing annual NFPA 25 fire pump testing. At least two recent projects of similar scope and complexity. Qualifications of personnel who would perform the testing. Sample annual fire pump testing report. Calibration documentation or description of testing equipment. Confirmation of ability to complete the required services at the Castle Point Campus. Identification of any subcontractors proposed for testing activities and their qualifications. Special Notice to SDVOSBs and VOSBs The Government is particularly interested in responses from: Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSBs) HUBZone Small Businesses Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSBs) Small Businesses Firms claiming SDVOSB or VOSB status should identify their certification status and applicable SBA certification information in their response. Response Submission Interested firms shall submit responses electronically no later than: November 2, 2026, at 10:00 AM Eastern Time Submit responses to: Natalie Acevedo Contract Specialist Department of Veterans Affairs Email: Natalie.Acevedo@va.gov Emilyne Armendariz Contract Specialist Department of Veterans Affairs Email: Emilyne.Armendariz@va.gov Subject Line: Sources Sought Response 36C24227Q0094 Annual NFPA 25 Fire Pump Inspection and Performance Testing Disclaimer This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for market research purposes. This notice does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP). The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation or award a contract as a result of this notice. title: C1DA--NRM A/E- 528A7-27-112 Fire Alarm Panel Upgrade
description: This is a "REQUEST FOR INFORMATION" only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government, and no contract will be awarded from this notice. Responses to this Sources Sought notice must be in writing. The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking qualified Architect-Engineer (A/E) firms to provide complete design and cost estimation services to upgrade the existing obsolete Edwards EST-3 fire alarm system (Project No. 528A7-24-112) at the Syracuse VA Medical Center located at 800 Irving Avenue, Syracuse, NY 13210. Work includes upgrading the existing fire alarm control panels and remote annunciators, installing a new fiber loop network connecting all panels and a new master control panel, expanding the addressable system to additional campus buildings, removing the existing fireman telephone system, and developing a phasing plan that maintains continuous fire alarm protection throughout construction. The A/E shall prepare complete working drawings, specifications, and detailed cost estimates, and provide construction period services. All drawings must be stamped by a registered Fire Protection Engineer (FPE), and the prime firm must have an FPE on staff no exceptions. Design shall comply with the latest editions of NFPA 70, NFPA 72, and the NEC, as well as applicable VA construction standards and fire protection design criteria. The NAICS Code is 541330 Engineering Services", with a size standard of $25.5M. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the Syracuse VA Medical Center. Please send all inquiries to: Ryan.Seburn@va.gov by 10:00 EST November 3rd, 2026. Phone calls will not be accepted.

title: Q601--Health Care Clearinghouse 1 - HIPAA Electronic Transactions and Insurance Discovery (VA-27-00018291) | Maxel/Svendsen
description: SPECIAL NOTICE NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE Electronic Insurance Transactions and Insurance Discovery HCCH I RFI eCMS ACTION NUMBER 36C24C27Q0007 October 29, 2026 Introduction: The Veteran s Health Administration (VHA) Office of Community Care (OCC), Revenue Operations (RO), eBusiness Solutions Office is looking to establish a Contract with a second Health Care Clearinghouse (HCCH) to continue to increase connectivity and further decrease processing time for VHA revenue operations. The Contractor shall conduct Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Health Care Eligibility/Benefit Inquiry and Response 270/271 electronic transactions received from our Austin Financial Services Center (FSC) from across the United States and its territories. The Contractor shall conduct customized electronic transactions to search for patient insurance when VHA does not already have information on file. The Contractor shall assist the VHA in continuing its mission to implement electronic transactions. At no time shall the Contractor direct, change, or engage in the formulation of VHA policy. The VHA is solely responsible to review the Contractor s recommendations and to make decisions concerning the formulation of policy. Background: As a Health Care Provider, VHA has initiated several projects to increase the number of transactions that are completed electronically to comply with legislation and to facilitate administrative simplification. The VHA currently utilizes a Contractor to transmit its incoming and outgoing electronic transactions to the national Payer community. Various transaction formats are utilized, such as HIPAA Health Care Claim 837 (X12N-5010) and National Council for Prescription Drug Program (NCPDP) transactions. VHA transactions are completed as batch and real-time transfers. This secondary Contract will transmit only HIPAA Health Care Eligibility/Benefit Inquiry and Response 270/271 transactions for various Payers. VHA intends to use this secondary HCCH to expand its access to significant payers not provided by our primary HCCH contract. In January 2018, VHA implemented an insurance coverage discovery process to identify patient insurance information when VA does not already have billable insurance information already on file. This new system provides a standard, automated method for obtaining patient s third-party insurance information by utilizing customized HIPAA transactions. VHA intends to continue utilizing a secondary HCCH to transmit these customized electronic transactions to identify patient insurance information. eBusiness Solutions, as a proponent of administrative simplification, currently exchanges transactions from health care entities to third-party carriers. VHA has a fully developed and robust system to generate insurance eligibility inquiries for all places of care throughout VHA and route the transactions through (FSC) prior to transfer to the HCCH. This system and processes are referred to as Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) electronic Insurance Verification (eIV) module. While required by law, at times VHA finds that patients are sometimes reluctant or remiss in sharing their third-party insurance information with VHA. To comply with federal regulations and to ensure revenue operations are generating health care claims to the maximum extent possible, VHA has engaged in efforts to seek patient s third-party insurance information from contracted sources. VHA has a fully developed a robust system of data extracts that provide basic patient demographics routed through FSC prior to transfer to the HCCH for which the Contractor can use to search for patient insurance information. This system and processes are referred to as Electronic Insurance Coverage Discovery (EICD). Notice of Intent to Sole Source: The Regional Procurement Office - Central Supplies & Services Team 2 intends to enter into a sole source procurement for the purchase of Electronic Insurance Transactions and Insurance Discovery HCCH I with: PNT Data Corporation Statutory Authority Permitting Other than Full and Open Competition: 41 USC §3304(a)(5), 38 U.S. Code § 8127(c), as implemented by FAR 6.302-5 (Authorized or Required by Statute). COs may use the non-competitive (sole source) procedures authorized in VAAR 819.7008, Sole Source Awards to a certified service-disabled veteran owned small business. The NAICS code for this procurement is 518210 (Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services) and the Small Business Administration Size Standard is $40 million Submittal Information: This notice of intent to is not a request for competitive quotes. However, any responsible source who believes it is capable of meeting the requirements may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which may be considered by the agency, only if received by the closing date and time of this notice. Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Respondents must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. Firms may register with SAM at https://www.sam.gov. description: Met deze aanbesteding wil opdrachtgever met één (1) contractant tot een raamovereenkomst komen voor het leveren en vervangen van ongeveer 10.000 paaltoparmaturen en 7.000 kofferarmaturen. Aanleiding hiervoor is dat een aanzienlijk deel van de openbare verlichting van de gemeente in de periode t/m 2030 grootschalig wordt vervangen of opgewaardeerd. Dit betekent het vervangen van bestaande armaturen door nieuwe led-armaturen. Dit zal worden vertaald in projecten die worden uitgevoerd op basis van deze raamovereenkomst. Met deze aanbesteding wil opdrachtgever met één (1) contractant tot een raamovereenkomst komen voor het leveren en vervangen van ongeveer 10.000 paaltoparmaturen en 7.000 kofferarmaturen. De geraamde waarde van de raamovereenkomst bedraagt op basis van regulier beschikbaar budget en historische gegevens van opdrachtgever ongeveer € 2.950.000,00 excl. btw, per jaar. Bij een looptijd van de raamovereenkomst van vier (4) jaar en zes (6) maanden komt dit neer op € 13.500.000,00 excl. btw. Hieraan kunnen inschrijvers geen rechten ontlenen.

title: Germany – Repair and maintenance services of security and defence materials – BG_1707_EU/26 - Werksinstandsetzung von diversen Sichtgeräten des Systems GTK Boxer
description: Der Auftrag umfasst die Werksinstandsetzung von diversen Sichtgeräten des Systems GTK Boxer. Die Bieter müssen im Rahmen der Angebotsabgabe berücksichtigen, dass die Angaben zu den jeweiligen Fachlosen lediglich aus den Vergangenheitswerten abgeleitete Schätzbedarfe sind sowie einen gegebenenfalls auftretenden Mehrbedarf (Sicherheitszuschlag) enthalten. Die tatsächlichen während der Vertragslaufzeit erfolgenden Beauftragungen können hinsichtlich der in einem Fachlos enthaltenen Bedarfsmengen der jeweiligen Versorgungsnummern abweichen. Die Obergrenze für den jeweiligen Auftrag bildet in jedem Fall die in dem betreffenden Fachlos zusammengefasste Gesamtmenge (Schätzbedarf + Sicherheitszuschlag). Eine Verpflichtung des AG, Einzelaufträge zu erteilen, wird durch diesen Vertrag nicht begründet. Die Vertragslaufzeit beginnt mit Zuschlagserteilung und endet nach 4 Jahren. title: Q301--Blood Donor Panel Testing for Captain James A. Lovell Federal Health Care Center (FHCC)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS The Department of Veterans Affairs is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support a requirement for Blood Don Services for the following Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 12 facility: Captain James A. Lovell Federal Health Care Center (FHCC) in North Chicago, IL. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 621511 Medical Laboratories. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. Requirements: Provide blood donor panel testing services to meet regulations set forth by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Association for the Advancement of Blood & Biotherapies (AABB), College of American Pathologists (CAP), The Joint Commission (TJC), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Center for Disease Control (CDC) and Prevention, and Department of Defense Instruction (DoD Inst). See Statement of Work on the following page for details. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, Web site address if applicable, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort and documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES, SOLE SOURCED OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice by 10:00am Local (Central) Time on November 3, 2026. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice must be emailed to joni.dorr@va.gov. Statement of Work Blood Donor Panel Testing Captain James A. Lovell Federal Health Care Center (FHCC), located at 3001 Green Bay Road, North Chicago, IL requires blood donor panel testing services, as detailed in the Blood Donor Panel Testing section, to meet regulations set forth by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Association for the Advancement of Blood & Biotherapies (AABB), College of American Pathologists (CAP), The Joint Commission (TJC), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Center for Disease Control (CDC) and Prevention, and Department of Defense Instruction (DoD Inst). The Contract shall be a five (5) year Ordering Period with five (5) one-year priced periods to be tasked off of at the discretion of the Government. SCOPE Contractor shall provide all labor, expenses, materials, tools, test equipment, analytical testing, supervision, expertise, and travel necessary to provide blood donor panel testing services. Any and all travel required by the Contractor to complete blood donor panel testing shall be covered by this Contract and shall not be separately charged to the Government. CONTRACT ORDER PERIOD Contract shall be a five (5) year Ordering Period with five (5) one-year priced periods. Priced Period 1: 03/01/2027-02/29/2028 Priced Period 2: 03/01/2028-02/28/2029 Priced Period 3: 03/01/2029-02/28/2030 Priced Period 4: 03/01/2030-02/28/2031 Priced Period 5: 03/01/2031-02/29/2032 CONFORMANCE STANDARDS AND LICENSURE Contractor shall continuously hold current and valid Government licenses, permits, and approvals as required by FDA, CAP, Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA), AABB, and/or other State regulatory agencies as it pertains to transporting/testing samples, and the reporting of specified tests to include infectious diseases, as appropriate, and as mandated by federal and state statutes. Contractor shall maintain valid certifications during the performance period of this Contract. All current permits, licenses, and certifications copies of the Contractor and if applicable, subcontractor shall be provided via email to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) or designee(s) upon award and upon recertification, if applicable. Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer s Representative (COR) or designee(s) in writing within twenty-four (24) hours, upon its loss of any required certification, accreditation or licensure. Contractor shall ensure its employees have the ability to perform the applicable duties consistent with their license and certification and ensure all laboratory testing staff comply with minimum Federal, State, and local law qualifications and requirements. Contractor shall ensure all testing and supervisory personnel at all Contractor-owned, affiliate, or subcontracted laboratories assigned to work under this contract meet and maintain the applicable personnel qualifications set forth under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) of 1988 regulations, the College of American Pathology (CAP) accreditation standards, or other accrediting organizations and State standards. title: DoWEA- Super Intelligence (SI) Education Support Solution
description: 1.Disclaimer The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) issuing this Sources Sought in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 to conduct market research. This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes. This is not a solicitation or Request for Proposal (RFP). This notice does not commit the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. The purpose of this notice is to determine the availability and capability of qualified small business concerns to provide a commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) Super Intelligence (SI)-enabled educational support solution supporting DoWEA operations in Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) locations. Please note that vendors are required to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at the time an offer/quotation/proposal is due to comply with the annual representations and certifications requirements. Therefore, only businesses with an active SAM registration will be eligible to receive any resultant contract(s) with the Department of War Education Activity. 2.Background DoWEA requires an enterprise-scale, COTS Super Intelligence (SI)-enabled educational support solution for grades 3-8�covering approximately 30,200 students and 6,000 educators�to measurably improve student learning outcomes and engagement while significantly reducing teacher preparation and administrative workloads. 3. Scope (Draft) The contractor shall provide a highly configurable, standards-aligned SI educational support solution across the following core functional areas: Task 1: Student-Facing SI Learning Assistant (Student Assistant) Pedagogical Design: Evidence-based SI tutoring utilizing scaffolded learning supports to guide students toward answers without direct generation of solutions. Feedback: Adaptive, real-time feedback dynamically linked to individual student mastery criteria. Overreliance Safeguards: Configurable session limits and system guardrails preventing wholesale answer generation for graded assignments. Standards Alignment: Real-time, dynamic alignment with DoWEA's Curriculum Standards. Safety & Persona Rules: Enforced age-appropriate content controls. The system shall not adopt names, conversational personas, romantic/companion behaviors, or humanlike characteristics. Accessibility: Full compliance with WCAG 2.2 Level AA and Section 508. Access Control: Teacher-gated/assignment-gated usage control modes. Task 2: Teacher-Facing SI Instructional Assistant (Teacher Assistant) Approval-Gated Feedback: Grade and score releases are strictly restricted to manual, explicit teacher verification (digital signature, click, or toggle). Oversight Dashboard: Real-time visibility (? 5s latency) of student usage patterns, misconceptions, overreliance flags, and student safety alerts. Instructional & Assessment Drafts: Dynamic generation of editable standards-aligned lesson plans, rubrics, quizzes, and parent newsletters. Content Library & Uploads: Curated repositories of prompt templates alongside frictionless, active-tab upload functionality. Interactive Student View: Built-in simulation toggle allowing teachers to model the interface to students. Task 3: Student, Parent, and Community Engagement Features Plain-language transparency notices detailing system strengths, limitations, and the role of human oversight. Staff- and family-facing privacy protection guides addressing student data storage and explicit prohibitions on the commercial use of student data. Orientation resources customized for digital citizenship, ethical use, and responsible learning support at home. Task 4: Professional Learning (PL) Delivery of regional role-based training (including four 1-hour synchronous webinars across Americas, Europe, and Pacific within the first 90 days). Train-the-trainer self-directed and facilitator-led micro-learning libraries (slides, handouts, guides). Virtual conference support for up to two annual DoWEA-sponsored conferences. Task 5: Efficacy Evaluation and Continuous Improvement Periodic measurements of student learning indicators, engagement, and teacher time savings. Collaboration with independent evaluators, including secure delivery of fully de-identified data extracts. Submission of Semiannual Improvement Reports (due every January and July). 4. System Integration & Compliance Constraints Security & Cloud Vetting: Solution must satisfy FedRAMP Level 2 standard equivalency. Data & SSO Integrations: Seamless interoperability with Schoology (LMS), Aspen (SIS), and Single Sign-On via ClassLink using industry standards (OAuth 2.0, SAML, LTI, OneRoster, and RESTful APIs). Strict Security & Privacy Policies: Full compliance with FERPA, COPPA, NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-122, and DoWEA AI 6600.01. Personnel Citizenship: 100% of personnel (including third-party PEN and security testers) with access or potential access to DoWEA PII or CUI must be U.S. Citizens or U.S. Persons. Encryption Standards: All data secured with TLS encryption in transit and AES-256 at rest. Secure database hosting strictly in United States data centers. 5. Potential NAICS Code The Government is considering the following NAICS codes: 513210 � Software Publishers (formerly 511210) 6. Contract Characteristics (Estimated) Enterprise-Scale Solution: Globally dispersed user base. Strict Performance Metrics: High-stakes AQLs (e.g., zero unauthorized grading/feedback releases, zero guardrail bypasses). Potential Contract Type: TBD (e.g., FFP, hybrid, or task order) evaluated under Best Value Trade-Off factors (Technical, Past Performance, Price). 7. Small Business Participation The Government is particularly interested in responses from: Small Business concerns 8(a) Small Business HUBZone Small Business Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) 8. Requested Information Interested vendors should submit a capability statement (maximum 10 pages) addressing the following: Company Information: Company name, address, UEI number, CAGE code, and socioeconomic size status. Relevant Experience: Experience deploying enterprise educational or SI software, supporting K-12 school systems, or collaborating with federal agencies (DoWEA). Technical Capabilities: System functionality overview, integration capability, and hosting/cybersecurity compliance. Staffing and Security: Personnel vetting approach, liaison qualifications, and global time-zone support capabilities. Contract Vehicles: Existing GWACs, GSA schedules, or other IDIQs. 9.Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Please submit a non-binding ROM cost estimate based on the draft scope. This estimate is for planning purposes only and will not be considered a formal quote. Please see the RFI-Sources Sought Notice for more details. 10.Submission Instructions Submissions and inquiries pertaining to this RFI must be sent electronically to Jiabao.Peng@dodea.edu and Karin.Werner@dodea.edu no later than 11:00AM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 03 November 2026. Vendor�s email message shall state �HE125427SI� in the subject line. Telephone calls regarding this RFI will not be accepted.

title: DNWP0016 - WAGR Enabling Works and Strip-out - Sellafield - A2R JV
description: WAGR Overview and Site Information The Windscale Advanced Gas-cooled Reactor (WAGR), commissioned in 1962, was the prototype for the UK's second-generation Advanced Gas-cooled Reactor (AGR) fleet. The facility (Building B50), recognised by its distinctive spherical containment shell, was supported by the fuel assembly building (B52) and turbine hall (B55). Following reactor core dismantling and removal in 2012, the WAGR Complex entered Care and Maintenance (C&M). The facility is now progressing towards its final phase of decommissioning and demolition. Existing records confirm the presence of Low-Level Waste (LLW) and Intermediate-Level Waste (ILW), resulting in ongoing radiological and contamination hazards. All buildings within the WAGR area are owned by the Remediation operating unit, remain under active surveillance and maintenance, and are classified as Beta Gamma contamination facilities. Project Scope The scope comprises enabling, strip-out, waste management and decommissioning support activities across the WAGR facility, alongside support for wider Windscale decommissioning programmes and emergent operational requirements. Key activities include (see attachment) - Strip-out Works: Internal and external removal of fixtures, fittings, equipment and non-structural elements to facilitate future decommissioning and demolition activities. - Radiological Waste Management: Safe handling, removal and management of LLW and ILW in accordance with site requirements. - Asset Reinstatement: Delivery of asset reinstatement works and provision of SQEP resources to support successful handover. - Pre-Construction Information (PCI): Support information gathering and site characterisation where existing PCI is insufficient. - Surveys: Plan and undertake surveys to assess radiological, hazardous and operational conditions in support of future decommissioning works. - Project Enabling Works: Design, fabricate, trial and implement enabling solutions, equipment and materials to support project delivery. - Asbestos Management: Planning, sampling, monitoring and licensed asbestos removal where required. - Procurement: Procurement of materials, equipment and associated quality documentation. - Waste Management: Sorting, segregation, consolidation and disposal of current and historical wastes, including completion of documentation for transfer to Sellafield Waste Coordinators. - Emergent Works: Rapid response support to operations and maintenance teams for safety-critical issues. - Temporary Works: Management, design and construction of temporary works, including scaffolding, enclosures and other supporting structures. - Decontamination: Decontamination activities to support area declassification and radiological rollback. - Plant Modifications: Production of Plant Modification Proposals (PMPs) and associated documentation. - Scaffolding Services: Provision of scaffolding design, supply and installation resources as required. Additional information: https://www.linkedin.com/company/a2r-altrad-atkinsrealis-remediation https://www.gov.uk/government/news/sellafield-ltd-awards-high-hazard-risk-reduction-framework-contract

description: This notice is for market research purposes only. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SOURCES SOUGHT. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this notice or any follow-up information requests. The 366th Contracting Squadron at Mountain Home Air Force Base (MHAFB), Idaho, is seeking responsible contractors to compete via forthcoming Request for Quote (RFQ) for an installation project to develop a complete and fully functional design and construction package to demolish Dormitory 2425. The purpose of the RFI is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of the Small Business Community: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) to include the 8(a) Program, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone) Program, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Program, and Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) Program. The purpose of the notice is to stimulate the interest of the greatest number of prospective contractors in advance of the RFQ. Firm's expressed interest in submitting a response on FA489727QSS11, Demolish Dormitory 2425 Firm's statement describing its qualifications and capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity, including any relevant technical experience. Firm's Small business category (Small Business, Woman-Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business [SDB] to include the 8(a) Program, Historically Underutilized Business Zones [HUBZone], Service- Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business [SDVOSB]). Interested firms shall respond to this Sources Sought via email not later than 10:00 a.m. MST, November 3, 2026. All interest firms must be registered in SAM (www.sam.gov) to be eligible for award of Government contracts. Send responses to both emails listed below: Natasha Lizama Contract Specialist 366th Contracting Squadron/PKB Mountain Home AFB, ID. natasha.lizama.1@us.af.mil Colin Shoemake Contracting Officer 366th Contracting Squadron/PKB Mountain Home AFB, ID. colin.shoemake@us.af.mil

title: J059--Building Management System-Sole Source Intent
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT Description The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 21, intends to award a sole source contract to Johnson Controls, Inc. for maintenance, support, inspection, testing, monitoring, programming, repair, and related services for the Metasys Building Management System (BMS) located throughout the Northern California Health Care System. The proposed contract will consist of: One (1) twelve-month base period Four (4) one-year option periods The anticipated start date: February 01, 2027 Sole Source Rationale The Metasys Building Management System is a proprietary platform developed and maintained by Johnson Controls, Inc. The system integrates critical facility operations including heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC), environmental controls, alarms, and energy management functions essential to patient care and facility operations. Based on market research conducted by the Government, Johnson Controls has represented that it is the only authorized source capable of providing the required proprietary software support, system programming, firmware updates, technical services, and manufacturer-certified maintenance for the installed Metasys system within the Northern California Health Care System. Johnson Controls provided documentation supporting its sole-source position. Award to any source other than Johnson Controls could result in incompatibility with existing equipment, loss of manufacturer support, increased operational risk, and potential disruption to critical building management functions. Authority This procurement is being conducted under the authority of RFO 12.201(a) or RFO 6.103-1(b), Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, as applicable. Submission of Capability Statements This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can satisfy the requirement may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required proprietary Metasys Building Management System services without limitation and with full manufacturer authorization. Capability statements must be received no later than November 03, 2026, 10AM PST. Responses shall be submitted electronically to: James Postell Contracting Officer Department of Veterans Affairs Email: James.Postell@va.gov Disclaimer This notice is for informational purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The Government does not intend to pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. Responses will be evaluated solely to determine whether competitive procurement is feasible.

title: Construction IDIQ Contract, FLETC Charleston, SC
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. Project Title: Construction IDIQ Contract, FLETC Charleston, SC Solicitation Number: 70LCHS26RPFB00001 NOTICE: Interested vendors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for the solicitation and any subsequent amendments (if applicable). The solicitation is anticipated to be posted within 2-4 weeks, with proposal due approximately 30 calendar days after issuance. A site visit will be conducted, and vendors must respond promptly to allow sufficient time for base access processing. Site visit details and access instructions will be provided in the solicitation. The Government intends to award one (1) firm-fixed price Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for construction, additions, alterations, maintenance, and repairs at buildings and structures located at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC) in Charleston, South Carolina. Work will be performed through the issuance of individual task orders issued under the contract. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision, and quality control necessary to perform the work specified in the basic contract and individual task orders. The contract will include a 12-month base period, four 12-month option periods, and an optional six-month extension in accordance with FAR 52.217-8. The contract minimum guarantee is $50,000 and the maximum value is not-to-exceed $33,000,000.00 over the contract's life. For planning purposes only, the Government estimates approximately $6,000,000.00 in task orders annually; this amount is not guaranteed nor is the Government limited by this amount annually. Individual task orders are anticipated to range from approximately $2,000 to $1,500,000.00. Task orders may encompass multiple construction trades, including but not limited to architectural, mechanical, civil, structural, roofing, demolition, electrical, environmental support, carpentry, roadwork, painting, plumbing, and masonry. Task order pricing will be based on the most current R.S. Means Facility Construction Cost Data Book, adjusted using the Charleston, South Carolina, City Cost Index multiplier. The contractor's coefficient will be applied to the total adjusted bare costs for labor, materials, and equipment. This acquisition is set aside for HUBZone small business concerns. FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, will apply. The applicable limitations require the contractor to perform at least 15 percent (15%) of the cost of the contract, not including the cost of materials, with its own employees. The Government is anticipating significant subcontracting opportunities under this contract.

title: CMT Catered Meals
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation, quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation is being issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01 dated 13 Mar 2026. This solicitation number W91ZRS27QA001 is for the Connecticut Army National Guard (CTARNG). The USPFO for Connecticut intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price contract for CMT Catered Meals. This request is due by 03 November 2026 at 1:00 p.m. (Eastern Time). This solicitation is 100% small business set aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 311991 � (Perishable Prepared Food Manufacturing). The small business standard size for NAICS 311991 is 700 employees. Instructions to Offerors All questions shall be in writing. Questions may be faxed to Leslie Fedler at 860-386-4070 or emailed at leslie.a.fedler.civ@army.mil. Questions must be submitted No Later Than 30 October 2026. All quotes are due no later than 1:00 p.m. eastern time, 03 November 2026. Quotes may be faxed to Leslie Fedler at 860-386-4070 or emailed to leslie.a.fedler.civ@army.mil. It is your responsibility to make sure your quote is received. The fact that the contracting office did not receive your quote due to an error on the fax machine or email address does not change the due date or time. Basis for Award "The Government will award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Award will be made on an 'all or none' basis to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offeror. Tradeoffs will not be permitted. Quotes will be evaluated for technical acceptability, past performance acceptability, and price." Evaluation Process: "The Government intends to evaluate quotes by first sorting them from lowest price to highest price. The lowest-priced quote will then be evaluated for technical acceptability and past performance. If the lowest-priced quote is determined to be 'Technically Acceptable' and has 'Acceptable Past Performance,' award will be made to that offeror, and no further quotes will be evaluated." Factor 1: Technical Acceptability: "The technical quote will be evaluated on a pass/fail basis. To be rated Acceptable, the quote must clearly demonstrate a compliance approach that meets all requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS), specifically demonstrating the capability to distribute media across the required channels and networks." Factor 2: Past Performance: "Past Performance will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. To be rated Acceptable, the offeror must submit a minimum of two (2) references within the past three (3) years demonstrating similar scope, complexity, and NAICS 311991 relevance. Offerors with no relevant past performance history will receive a 'Neutral' rating, which will be treated as 'Acceptable' for award purposes." Factor 3: Price: "Price will be evaluated for mathematical completeness and price reasonableness. Award will be made to the lowest total priced, responsible offeror whose technical and past performance quotes are rated Acceptable." The Contracting Officer will evaluate products on the basis of information furnished by the offeror or identified in the offer and reasonably available to the Contracting Officer. The Contracting Officer is not responsible for locating or obtaining any information not identified in the offer. The Government is not responsible for developing the comparison from insufficient information provided. Must be Technical Acceptability" as meeting both the performance capability and statutory compliance with FAR 52.219-30 and 13 CFR 125.6. All Offerors must accept this as payment. The wide area workflow website is https://wawf.eb.mil/. The Government contract supersedes all other terms and agreements from any other vendor. description: Amendment 04 is attached to provide the answers to Industry's questions regarding this RFI. Attachment 2-RFI_M67854-26-I-4208_Official_QA_20261021_Public Release is provided in the attachments. No further extension will be provided beyond 03 November 2026. Amendment 03 is attached to revise the response due date from 19 October 2026 at 1:00 P.M. to 03 November 2026 at 1:00 P.M. Questions and answers are in final review and will be released in Amendment 04. Please see below for Market Research Clarifications. Market Research Clarification Statements: 1. Clarification on Primary Scope and Contractor-Provided Tooling: The Government reiterates that the primary requirement of this effort is the provision of skilled, professional IT touch-labor services (Objective 1). Any proposed AI/automation tooling must be presented as an embedded component of the service delivery model, consistent with the constraints in Section 3.2 of the RFI, designed to augment the workforce and improve efficiency. 2. Additional Request for Information on Service-Based Ordering Models: In addition to the areas outlined in the original RFI, the Government is seeking industry feedback on recommended ordering approaches for service-based delivery models. Respondents are encouraged to describe frameworks where the Government could procure "hours of service" or service outcomes rather than individual labor categories. Descriptions should include associated tooling considerations, structural elements that support efficient ordering, and methods for performance tracking. 3. Clarification on Submission Formatting: To resolve confusion identified in industry questions, respondents are instructed to adhere to the following: The "Capabilities Narrative" is limited to five (5) pages (PDF). Any optional "Supplementary Materials" are separate and limited to fifteen (15) pages (PDF). The "Vendor Comment Matrix" must be submitted in its native Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) format, and the 300-word limit per cell is in effect. 4. Clarification on ROM Pricing and Software Licensing: To resolve the conflict identified between RFI Section 3.2 and Area B, respondents are instructed that this is a services acquisition. Any costs associated with contractor-provided proprietary tooling (licensing, subscriptions, etc.) are expected to be included within the fully burdened labor rates of the "Labor" ROM component. The "Platform Licensing/Subscription" and "Variable/Consumption Costs" line items should be used only for estimating potential Government-incurred costs on Government-owned platforms (e.g., ServiceNow credits, Power Platform licensing). title: Request for Information/Market Intelligence Notice: Use of Progressive Design Build (PDB) with Other Transaction Authority (OTA) - Fort Hunter-Liggett Water System Improvements
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 237110 � Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small businesIntells regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction of a project to restore and modernize the potable water system and wastewater collection system throughout the Fort Hunter Liggett Installation. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary design services, equipment, materials, labor, construction management, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional and modernized potable water and wastewater systems on the Installation. The Fort Hunter Liggett water distribution system dates back to the 1950�s with a few areas believed to be even older and includes a three (3) well configuration that has sufficient pumping capacity to serve current supply demands, however, the water transmission system is undersized to satisfy the demand of the system. While the current water system storage may be sufficient for normal operation, it cannot sustain the system for more than one day in the event of a pump outage and/or fire flow event during maximum day conditions; therefore, additional system storage is necessary. A new Tank Farm with adequate storage capacity (estimated to be a minimum of 2 million gallons) to be determined and validated in accordance with NSPC, UFC, and NFPA criteria, should be in vicinity of security fence gate 10 (Lat: 35.997638� , Long: -121.224355�). Currently the primary storage tank for the potable water system is on the opposite side of the cantonment from the wells and the transmission main and distribution are combined causing significant pressure variations far in excess of industry standard, causing accelerated deterioration of system components. Many pipelines, valves, and hydrants within the distribution system have currently exceeded their useful life expectancy and have failed or failing. High operating pressures place additional strain on this aging system, requiring operational improvements as well as rehabilitation/replacement of existing assets. Modernizing SCADA components are necessary to increase efficiency and updated to cover any system revisions and future improvements. SCADA infrastructure improvements shall integrate into the existing SCADA infrastructure. Fort Hunter Liggett�s wastewater collection system was installed around the same time as the water potable system. Due to the age of the system and deterioration, replacement and rehabilitation of sanitary sewer lines, manholes, and the waste treatment plant lagoon are needed to return the system to be fully functional and code compliant. The wastewater treatment plant relies on a series of lagoons to treat sewage. There are lagoons that have operational deficiencies and require the replacement of the impermeable liner. In addition, the lagoon currently lacks baffles, which are essential for directing the flow of wastewater in a way that maximizes treatment time and prevents "short circuiting". Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $70-$80M PRIMARY ACQUISITION STRATEGY UNDER EVALUATION: Progressive Design Build (PDB) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Progressive Design Build (PDB) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority authorizes transactions other than standard contracts to carry out facility repair and construction projects � including planning, design, engineering, piloting and execution � enabling early contractor involvement, commercial pricing transparency, and schedule and cost efficiencies. Currently, the Government has advanced a conceptual design for the following potable water system features below. New transmission main to connect the existing well field to the main distribution system within the cantonment area. New storage infrastructure as required to satisfy requirements for fire safety, emergency needs, and operational storage. Upgrades to existing water supply wells to enhance water-supply reliability and redundancy. A Technical Assessment Report of the condition of Fort Hunter Liggett�s utilities systems and modernization recommendations of the water and sanitary sewer systems was completed in June 2024. The onsite assessments used in developing the Technical Assessment Report were conducted November 28-December 7, 2023. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing PDB utilizing an OT Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The PDB Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): The evaluation process for selection of the most highly qualified design-builder would be qualifications based. A streamlined, two-step Qualifications-Based Selection would occur: Step 1: White Papers/Statement of Qualifications submission. Step 2: Down selected design builders would be invited to Pitch Meetings/Presentations. Most highly qualified firm following pitch meetings would be selected to enter into negotiations. The OT Award would be two phases: Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): The Government team will negotiate the price of Agreement Phase I � Design and Pre-Construction Services with the selected design-builder. work collaboratively to advance the design, conduct open-book cost estimating, and mitigate project risks. Phase 2 (Construction): Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design (e.g., 60% to 90%), the Awardee will propose a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). If the GMP is accepted, the Government will exercise Phase 2 for construction execution. If a GMP cannot be agreed upon, the Government retains an "off-ramp" to complete the design and construct the facility via alternative methods INFORMATION REQUESTED Interested parties are requested to respond to the following questions to help shape the final acquisition strategy. Responses shall be made using the link or QR code in the attachment: Company Profile: Q1. Firm Name Q2. Address Q3. Point of Contact (Name, Title) Q4. Phone Number Q5. Email Address Q6. Participating Role (Prime Contractor, Subcontractor, Design Firm, Other) Other Transaction Authority (OTA) & Collaborative Delivery Experience: Q10. OTA Experience: Describe your firm's previous experience (if any) executing projects utilizing OTA. Q11. Collaborative Delivery Experience: Describe your experience executing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk), Progressive Design Build (PDB), Integrated Design and Construction (IDAC), Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) or other highly collaborative delivery methods. Fort Hunter Liggett Waterline Q12. Describe your experience/expertise with water and wastewater utility construction. Q13. Agency/Office Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) National Institutes of Health (NIH) Office of Logistics and Acquisition Operations (OLAO) Description The HHS/NIH/OLAO is seeking to obtain information regarding the availability of U.S. manufactured specialized disposable gloves. The HHS personnel including clinicians, researchers, laboratory personnel, animal care staff, maintenance personnel, and other staff who may encounter chemical, biological, clinical, research, animal care, facility, diagnostic, or related workplace hazards require specialized disposable gloves to safely perform their duties of clinical, research, diagnostic, laboratory, animal care, maintenance, decontamination, cleaning, waste handling, facility-support, and emergency preparedness activities that support the Department's mission. These gloves are a critical element of personal protective equipment for personnel who handle or may respond to a national or international incident that would result I their contact with hazardous chemicals, biological materials, infectious or potentially infectious substances and diseases, contaminated surfaces, research specimens, animal-related materials, cleaning and disinfecting agents, and other materials presenting exposure risks. Gloves must be appropriate for the specific hazards, environments, and tasks for which they are used. Glove performance is evaluated on hazard-specific protective characteristics, including material, thickness, barrier integrity, chemical resistance, degradation resistance, permeation performance, durability, dexterity, fit, tactile sensitivity, puncture or tear resistance, and compatibility with the intended task. Chemical Applications - Gloves should be supported, where available, by product-specific chemical resistance documentation for the material and thickness being procured. Such documentation typically includes permeation testing (ASTM F739 or equivalent), which establishes how long a glove resists breakthrough by a given chemical, and degradation testing (ASTM D471, ANSI/ISEA 105, or equivalent), which establishes whether the glove material physically deteriorates on contact. Gloves used with chemotherapy agents or other hazardous drugs should have documented resistance under ASTM D6978 or an equivalent standard, which assesses permeation specifically by chemotherapy drugs. Basis for Award "The Government will award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Factor 2: Past Performance: "Past Performance will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. The purpose of this RFI is to: Gather information from industry regarding the general approach, feasibility, staffing models, and anticipated cost of performing the type of work described in the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS); Obtain industry recommendations regarding potential prioritization, phasing, scaling, or restructuring of the contemplated work; Assess the relationship between the contemplated scope, anticipated resource requirements, and likely market pricing; and Inform ACL/AoD's decisions regarding scope, task structure, phasing, and acquisition strategy as the PWS is finalized. The draft PWS provided with this RFI is for market research purposes only and remains subject to revision. Respondents should not assume that the final scope, task structure, deliverables, or performance standards in the PWS will appear in any resulting solicitation. The Government is specifically interested in industry feedback that identifies where the described scope may be too broad, too narrow, under-resourced, or structured in a way that drives unnecessary cost, so that the requirement can be refined prior to release of a solicitation. BACKGROUND The Administration on Disabilities (AoD), within ACL/HHS, is responsible for administering the Developmental Disabilities Assistance and Bill of Rights Act of 2000 (DD Act), which establishes the National Network of University Centers for Excellence in Developmental Disabilities Education, Research, and Service (UCEDDs). AoD is considering a contract vehicle to provide network-wide training, technical assistance (TA), and capacity-building support to UCEDD. Through this RFI, the Government seeks industry feedback concerning the feasibility, resource requirements, potential cost drivers, and appropriate structure of the contemplated requirement. The Government is also interested in identifying opportunities to prioritize, phase, scale, or otherwise structure the work to achieve program objectives efficiently. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDENTS Interested parties are requested to submit a written response of no more than seven (7) pages, excluding the cover page. Please include in your response: Company name, address, point of contact, phone, email, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), if the respondent elects to provide it; Business size, applicable socioeconomic status (small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.) and applicable NAICS code(s) under which your firm is classified; Provide a brief description of the organization�s capabilities and relevant experience performing comparable technical assistance, capacity-building, evaluation, knowledge management, or technology support contracts, particularly any involving disability networks, university-based centers, HHS/ACL, or similarly structured federal TA contracts; and Responses to the questions below. RFI QUESTIONS Respondents are encouraged to provide concise, specific information directly responsive to the questions below. Marketing materials or general corporate information that does not address the contemplated requirement are not necessary. Interested and capable organizations are requested to address the following questions: Based on the draft PWS, describe whether the contemplated scope appears feasible and identify any tasks, deliverables, performance requirements, or assumptions that may create significant performance, staffing, schedule or cost risk. Identify any areas of the draft requirement that industry recommends clarifying, restructuring, consolidating, or otherwise revising; Describe the general staffing model and categories of labor or expertise that would reasonably be required to perform the contemplated work. Identify any specialized expertise, staffing assumptions, or other resources that would materially affect performance or cost; Provide a rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimate of annual cost to perform the general scope described in the PWS, and the basis for that estimate. The ROM is requested solely for acquisition planning and market research purposes. Please identify the significant assumptions and primary cost drivers underlying the estimate; Provide recommendations on which elements of the contemplated scope should be prioritized, phased, scaled, or consolidated to achieve the greatest programmatic value without materially affecting the overall objectives of the requirement. Respondents may recommend alternative approaches or scope adjustments that could improve efficiency, reduce cost, or enhance the likelihood of successful performance; Based on the technology related functions contemplated in the draft PWS, describe, the technology approach your organization would propose for supporting the Core Functions Dashboard and AI-assisted chatbot (e.g., existing commercial/Government-authorized platforms vs. custom development), including anticipated cost drivers, timeline, and relevant privacy/security/accessibility (Section 508) considerations; and Based on the nature of the contemplated services, identify and recommendations regarding acquisition structure or contract type that the Government should consider. Respondents may address, as applicable: Fixed-price, cost-reimbursement, time-and-materials, labor-hour, or hybrid approaches; Use of a single contract or other acquisition structure; Task organization or phasing approaches; and Any acquisition structure that could reduce performance risk, administrative burden, or unnecessary cost. Recommendations should include a brief explanation of the underlying rationale. Submission Instructions: Responses must be submitted electronically to Khaled.Gohar@hhs.gov no later than November 03, 2026, 2:00 PM ET. Responses should reference RFI - UCEDD Technical Assistance in the subject line. Proprietary information must be clearly marked. Respondents should avoid including proprietary or confidential information unless it is necessary to meaningfully respond to the RFI. The Government may use information submitted in response to the RFI for market research and acquisition planning purposes, including refinement of the requirement and acquisition strategy. Consistent with the revised Buy Indian Act, HHS/IHS adopted the definition of an Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) set forth in 48 CFR 1480.201. This definition includes the following requirement, amongst others: "the Indians or Indian Tribes must, together, receive at least a majority of the earnings from the contract." Instructions for submission are outlined further below. Estimated Value: The estimated value of this requirement, if all four option periods are exercised, is approximately $750,000 over the five-year period of performance, based on preliminary Government estimates. This estimate is provided for informational purposes only and is subject to change. 1. Purpose of Notice This Sources Sought Notice is issued in accordance with the Buy Indian Act, 25 U.S.C. � 47, and its implementing regulations, to conduct market research and determine the availability and interest of qualified Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs) and Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) capable of providing the supplies/services described below. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submission of information does not guarantee that a solicitation for this requirement will be issued, nor does it obligate the Government to award any resulting contract. At the Sources Sought stage, the Government is assessing general firm capability, experience, and interest � not evaluating specific personnel. Personnel qualification requirements, if any, will be addressed in a future solicitation, should one be issued. This Sources Sought Notice does not commit the Government to any particular acquisition strategy. 2. Background / Requirement Description The Billings Area Indian Health Service (BAIHS), Blackfeet Service Unit (BFSU), provides comprehensive healthcare services to American Indian and Alaska Native beneficiaries residing on and near the Blackfeet Indian Reservation in Browning, Montana. The Blackfeet Community Hospital requires continued access to dental oral and maxillofacial surgery services to meet the clinical needs of its patient population. Teaming/Subcontracting: If your firm intends to team with or subcontract to another entity to meet the requirement, identify the proposed teaming partner(s) and the anticipated division of work. Statement of Interest: A brief statement confirming your firm's interest in and capability to compete for this requirement if a solicitation is issued. 6. Instructions for Submission Questions shall be submitted electronically to Prudence.YellowOwl@ihs.gov no later than 12noon Tuesday, October 27, 2026. Answers will be posted to sam.gov no later than Thursday October 29, 2026. Responses shall be submitted electronically to Prudence.YellowOwl@ihs.gov by 12:30 PM Mountain Time, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, limited to 10 pages (PDF, 12-point font), and must include a completed Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) representation form; responses missing the IEE form may not be considered. Responses will not be returned and will not be publicly posted. All information marked as proprietary or confidential will be treated accordingly to the extent permitted by law. 7. title: SOURCES SOUGHT: COMMERCIAL AVAILABLILITY OF FULLY AUTOMATED CLEAN SHOP WET PROCESS SYSTEM AND ASSOCIATED EQUIPMENT B794 NAS JAX, FL
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET SURVEY FOR WRITTEN INFORMATION ONLY, TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL COMMERCIAL AVAILABLILITY OF FULLY AUTOMATED CLEAN SHOP WET PROCESS SYSTEM AND ASSOCIATED EQUIPMENT FOR THE DESIGN- BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, RENOVATION OF B794 CLEANING SHOP, AT NAVAL AIR STATION (NAS) JACKSONVILLE, FL THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The reference number for this posting is N6945027RB794. This is a market research tool being used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential sources that can manufacture and install a fully automated clean shop wet process system and associated equipment. Project Description: The procurement for B794 encompasses design, engineering and construction services, along with the integration of personal property and transition services necessary for the renovation of the Cleaning Shop, located within existing B794 at NAS Jacksonville, FL. New equipment will be integrated and work cohesively as a system. Each cleaning line in the system must be equipped with two bridge-crane-style material transporters that have enclosed canopy-style ventilation with three process lines, programmed to work together. The lines should be compact with less than 6� between each tank. The cleaning lines must have dedicated spray rinse tanks and manual spray cleaning booths that are incorporated into the line. Transporting the components for processing must be done in 3-axis: Vertical (Lifting), Horizontal (Lateral), and Horizontal (Longitudinal). The automated cleaning line shall be a comprehensive system designed to clean aircraft components, record data, and report errors to operators of the system. The unit must operate in limited production space and requires control integration to properly process the needed production. The contractor must demonstrate experience with this specific type of cleaning lines: compact (width restrictions with tanks being less than 6� apart; ventilation hoods cannot be used with space constraints), fully automated, with canopy style hood ventilation on the material transporter with hard ducting. The cleaning system must work as a unit and be controlled from its own Human Machine Interface (HMI) or a central master supervisory HMI/SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) station that coordinates automated material transporters and line handoffs across all three lines. Integrated systems are: Heavy-duty cleaning lines Titanium cleaning line Vapor degreasers Associated support and ancillary process equipment The cleaning equipment must utilize a canopy-style hooded material transporter to eliminate the amount of exhaust air. This must reduce the energy consumption of the line to the required level while also improving environmental air emissions. The system must use ducting that does not flex and is not prone to heavy maintenance requirements or fatigue failures. To maintain consistency, quality, reliability, and deliverability, the equipment for the clean shop renovation should utilize products that have been designed and proven to work in the industry for over 5 years with experience that will allow integration of multiple cleaning products.
