title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YT-812
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF) is conducting market research to determine industry capability and interest in performing the maintenance, repair, and preservation of YT-812. Work will be accomplished at the Contractor's facility. The Government is seeking responses from sources that can perform the following work. Geographical Area of consideration: To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. YT-812 � Length: 90 FT � Width: 38 FT � Age: 4 YRS � Hull Type: Steel � Draft: 16 FT � Full Displacement: 494 L Tons � Light Load: 438 L Tons Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractor�s facility. The Government will transport the vessel to the Contractor�s repair facility. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Replace zinc and impressed anodes. Blast and preserve underwater hull and freeboard, bulwarks, and handrails. Blast and preserve main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck non-skid. Perform hull and freeboard Ultrasonic Test (UT) inspections. Perform hull and freeboard, main deck, 1st deck, and 2nd deck Visual Inspections (VT). Repair hull and winch valves. Repair deckhouse expansion joint. Open, pump, clean, inspect and test CHT, ballast, potable water, fuel oil, waste oil and day tanks. Preserve, disinfect and certify the potable water tank. Onload fuel. Repair HVAC thermostat. Replace deck winch, mast, and brow systems hydraulic hoses. Accomplish 1- and 5-year interval inspection and repair requirements for port and starboard Schottel Z-drive units. Accomplish repairs to the port and starboard twin disc transmission coolers. Accomplish winch control piping modification (YT808-0104D), air piping modification (YT808-0105D), potable water hose bibb drain valve installation (YT808-0107D), and automatic voltage regulator installation (YT808-0109D). Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Upon completion of all work the Government will take custody of the vessel. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Please hand or digitally sign your letter of interest and e-mail it to the Government contacts listed below, with " Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YT-812 Sources Sought Response" in the subject field. title: P8-A Ground Station (PGS) Aircraft Media Gateway (AMG) Production, Installation and Sustainment Support
description: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. REQUIREMENTS: Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) PMA-290 P-8A program office has a requirement for additional quantities of ground systems hardware and software in support of the P-8A I3B2 aircraft and legacy aircraft. This effort will provide continued modifications and installs of P-8A Ground Station (PGS) systems, and other support for Mobile Mission Systems to include Poseidon Quick Look (PQL) and Fly Away Kit (FAK). The contractor�s effort will also include associated support activities and other direct costs (ODCs). This action does not introduce new mission areas or fundamentally new capabilities. The requested information is to assist the Government in conducting market research to determine potential business sources that have the assets, skills, experience, financial stability, qualifications, and knowledge required to support the above request. Include a statement regarding industrial security clearance. This Sources Sought is not, however, a request for inquiries concerning subcontracting opportunities. AMG is integrated within P-8A Ground Stations (PGS) for media building purposes to support missions for P-8A Block I and Block II aircraft. The anticipated period of performance for this effort is Q2FY27 through Q1FY30. SUBMISSION DETAILS: Interested persons may submit a Capability Statement identifying their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. Only Capability Statements received on or before 15 calendar days after the posting date of this Notice will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this Notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability Statements received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Capability Statements submitted should be pertinent and specific in the technical/management/business area under consideration, on each of the following qualifications. Small/Large Business Status: A company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), DUNS Number, CAGE Code, and a statement regarding current small/large business status. Technical Data/ Computer Software Documentation: Since the Government does not possess sufficient technical data that a Contractor would require in order for that Contractor to fulfill the planned requirements, each interested party must demonstrate that its company currently possesses or has authorized access to the necessary technical data, computer software and computer software documentation, or has a viable plan to obtain, generate, or otherwise secure authorized access to the necessary technical data, computer software and computer software documentation; and that it will be maintained throughout the duration of the effort being solicited. Execution: A description of the technical approach for meeting the requirements of the contemplated procurements. If a small business, provide a description of the plan for ensuring that the small business performs at least 50% of the work itself in terms of cost of performance. Experience: A description of previous (awarded within last 3 years) or current relevant contracts. Personnel: Name, professional qualifications and specific experience of key personnel (e.g., program manager(s), project manager(s), technical lead(s), etc. Facilities: Availability and description of facilities and equipment that will be utilized to meet requirements. Security: A description of facility and personnel security regarding the handling and storage of classified information and hardware. The information submitted should address feasibility of performing the following task for integration with P-8A Ground Station (PGS): Description of the Contractor's approach in the sustainment of software and hardware of P-8A Ground Station (PGS) specifically for Aircraft Media Gateway (AMG) to support P-8A aircraft. Include specific relevant technical and management experience performed in the past five (5) years. Any other specific and pertinent information as pertains to this particular area of procurement that would enhance our consideration and evaluation of the Capability Statement. Interested parties are advised against submitting a Capability Statement that merely mimics information in this Notice, provides brochure-like information, or provides general information. Responses to this Notice are not to exceed 20 pages in length on 8.5 x 11-inch paper with one inch margins and font no smaller than 10 point Times New Roman. The Government requests that respondents deliver responses electronically via e-mail in Microsoft Word or PDF format with proper data markings for unclassified and proprietary information not later than 15 calendar days after the posting date of this Notice. Classified material SHALL NOT be submitted. All submissions shall include this Sources Sought Notice Reference Number, company name, company address, CAGE code, DUNS number, and a point-of-contact who is able to discuss the Capability Statement submitted. Point-of-contact information shall include name, position, phone number, and email address. Acknowledgement of receipt will be provided. All information submitted will be adequately safeguarded from unauthorized disclosure in accordance with FAR 15.207. All submissions must be clearly marked with the following caption: For Official Use Only, Releasable to Government Agencies for Evaluation Purposes Only. Responses that fail to comply with the above instructions or present ideas not pertinent to subject, may not be reviewed. All information received in response to this Notice that is marked proprietary will be handled accordingly. Information submitted in response to this Notice is submitted at no cost to the Government and will not be returned. The Government is under no obligation to provide responses or comments to information received from interested persons but may request additional information following review. Note: If the interested person is a foreign concern or if a U.S. interested person has a team member or partner who is a foreign entity, adherence to all International Traffic and Arms Regulations (ITAR) is required.

title: Barbados – Electrical power systems design services – Caribbean Electricity Integrator Facility
description: The Caribbean Electricity Integrator Facility (CEIF) will provide integrated technical, engineering and transaction-advisory support to advance priority electricity-integration investments in the Caribbean from analysis and project identification towards investment and tender readiness. The specific objective of the contract is to validate regional Caribbean electricity-interconnection options and prepare, through an integrator approach, a St Kitts and Nevis-anchored Northern Corridor package that can reach at least tender or contracting readiness where feasible, while developing a replicable mechanism for future Caribbean electricity-integration corridors. The initial focus will be on St Kitts and Nevis, including the interconnection between St Kitts and Nevis and the associated generation, grid and enabling infrastructure required to support a viable integrated electricity system. The assignment will also assess the potential extension of the Northern Corridor towards Antigua and Barbuda and other Northern Leeward receiving/readiness nodes, subject to technical, economic and commercial validation. The contractor will assess the relevant technical, economic, financial, legal, commercial, environmental, social, institutional and procurement dimensions and develop viable business, financing, risk-allocation and procurement structures for priority investments. The work will also support the development of a scale-up and replication mechanism for a wider pipeline of Caribbean electricity-integration investments. The direct beneficiaries and geographical focus will include Caribbean partner countries covered by the EU-Caribbean Cooperation Facility+ and, where relevant to the electricity-interconnection agenda, Caribbean Overseas Countries and Territories and French Outermost Regions, with the precise geographical scope of subsequent corridors to be determined through the analysis. The contractor will provide an engineering-anchored transaction advisory team, combining strong power-system, grid and submarine-interconnection capability with expertise in market and demand analysis, economics, financial structuring, legal and commercial design, procurement, environmental and social safeguards and stakeholder engagement.

description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The VA Enterprise Procurement Office intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) 36E79727R0007 for an unrestricted procurement for Sacubitril-Valsartan Tablets, for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) (inclusive of Consolidated Mail Order Pharmacies (CMOPs) and Option 2 State Veterans Homes (SVH)), Department of Defense (DoD) (inclusive of Tricare Mail Order Pharmacies (TMOPs)), Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Indian Health Service (IHS), and Federal Health Care Center (FHCC). VA will award one contract to the responsible offeror who will be able to provide an uninterrupted source of supply for the contracted items. The contract period will be for one year plus four pre-priced one-year option periods. The contract items will be distributed through the VA s and DOD s respective Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor Programs. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. Offerors must state the exact name (name that appears on label) by which the drug will be supplied and have an NDC number that is unique to the offeror. The successful offeror/contractor's label with its unique NDC shall be the only label on the product. Contractors shall not affix their label over another label on the product. VA labels must be able to securely adhere on top of the successful offeror/contractor s label. All unit of use packaging identified in the Schedule of Supplies, (60 & 180 count bottles) shall contain a safety-cap capable of having the outer part of the cap deshelled and / or a convertible cap to produce a non-safety cap and a bottle with a minimum required size of 120cc volume. The safety cap must not exceed the diameter of the bottle. The bottle must have a cylindrical body and minimum of 5.75 circumference. The bottle must fit a label with a dimension of 5.25 x 2 . The 0.5 additional space is required to keep the bar code exposed and/or allow for the display of the expiration date and lot number. Solicitation # 36E79727R0007 will be electronically issued in commercial item format in accordance with FAR Part 12 on or about December 18, 2026, with a tentative closing date of January 7, 2027. title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including:1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery.2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material.3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting.4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS).5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded. Please review and submit any questions related to this solicitation through the PIEE module link found down in the attachments section by October 19th. These questions and answers will be public. QandA will be closed after October 19th. Proposals shall be submitted through the solicitation module in PIEE. See the PIEE submittal instructions for directions on submitting proposal documents in PIEE. Any extensions to this solicitation will be posted here. title: ND NP THRO 204(1) Buck Hill Road
description: INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION WITH HUBZONE PREFERENCE PROJECT NUMBER: ND NP THRO 204(1) PROJECT NAME: Buck Hill Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Buck Hill Road, also known as Route 204, is located in Billings County within Theodore Roosevelt (THRO) National Park (NP) in the southeast portion of the park near the South Unit, Medora, ND. The route is located in mountainous terrain at approximate elevation of 2,500 to 2,800 feet. It begins at the intersection of Buck Hill Road and South Unit Scenic Loop Road. The route then proceeds southeasterly for approximately � of a mile and ascends approximately 300 feet vertically to the Buck Hill Overlook parking area. The route is located entirely within Theodore Roosevelt NP. There is one (1) base schedule and no options. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The project includes three major components; 1) Approximately � mile of roadway rehabilitation, 2) Approximately 1,000 linear feet of deep subexcavation to address an existing landslide, and 3) Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot. The main roadway rehabilitation includes pulverization of the existing roadway, placement of new roadway aggregate, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement and replacing existing guardrail with new guardrail. Additionally, this work includes constructing new paved ditches and installing concrete curb and gutter along most of the length of the roadway. This includes installation of several drainage inlets and culverts as well as new striping and signage. The deep subexcavation work includes removal of approximately existing unsuitable material to a 10 feet depth for a continuous 1,000 linear foot length of roadway and replacing with suitable material with geosynthetic reinforcement and installing subsurface drainage. A geotechnical report will be provided with the PS&E package. Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot expands and adds more parking spaces and accommodates larger trucks, recreational vehicles, and tour buses. The work includes removing the existing pavement, placing embankment material, new aggregate base, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement. This work also includes constructing accessible parking, placing new concrete sidewalk and curb and gutter, and striping and signage. New trash receptacles and stone benches will be installed as part of the new parking area. Buck Hill Road may be closed for the duration of construction. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: Approximate quantities for major work items: 11,000 cubic yards of subexcavation 1,000 linear feet of geocomposite sheet drain 2,000 tons of hot asphalt concrete pavement 5,000 tons of roadway aggregate 550 linear feet of 24-inch pipe culvert (thick walled HDPE, fused) 5,100 linear feet of concrete curb and gutter (tan and onyx colored) 650 square yards of concrete sidewalk (tan colored) 1,600 linear feet of guardrail ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement � October 2026 Award - January 2027 Construction � April 2027 through November 2027 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000

title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded. Please review and submit any questions related to this solicitation through the PIEE module link found down in the attachments section by October 19th. These questions and answers will be public. title: ND NP THRO 204(1) Buck Hill Road
description: INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION WITH HUBZONE PREFERENCE PROJECT NUMBER: ND NP THRO 204(1) PROJECT NAME: Buck Hill Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Buck Hill Road, also known as Route 204, is located in Billings County within Theodore Roosevelt (THRO) National Park (NP) in the southeast portion of the park near the South Unit, Medora, ND. The route is located in mountainous terrain at approximate elevation of 2,500 to 2,800 feet. It begins at the intersection of Buck Hill Road and South Unit Scenic Loop Road. The route then proceeds southeasterly for approximately � of a mile and ascends approximately 300 feet vertically to the Buck Hill Overlook parking area. The route is located entirely within Theodore Roosevelt NP. There is one (1) base schedule and no options. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The project includes three major components; 1) Approximately � mile of roadway rehabilitation, 2) Approximately 1,000 linear feet of deep subexcavation to address an existing landslide, and 3) Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot. The main roadway rehabilitation includes pulverization of the existing roadway, placement of new roadway aggregate, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement and replacing existing guardrail with new guardrail. Additionally, this work includes constructing new paved ditches and installing concrete curb and gutter along most of the length of the roadway. This includes installation of several drainage inlets and culverts as well as new striping and signage. The deep subexcavation work includes removal of approximately existing unsuitable material to a 10 feet depth for a continuous 1,000 linear foot length of roadway and replacing with suitable material with geosynthetic reinforcement and installing subsurface drainage. A geotechnical report will be provided with the PS&E package. Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot expands and adds more parking spaces and accommodates larger trucks, recreational vehicles, and tour buses. The work includes removing the existing pavement, placing embankment material, new aggregate base, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement. The route is located in mountainous terrain at approximate elevation of 2,500 to 2,800 feet. It begins at the intersection of Buck Hill Road and South Unit Scenic Loop Road. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The project includes three major components; 1) Approximately � mile of roadway rehabilitation, 2) Approximately 1,000 linear feet of deep subexcavation to address an existing landslide, and 3) Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot. The main roadway rehabilitation includes pulverization of the existing roadway, placement of new roadway aggregate, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement and replacing existing guardrail with new guardrail. Additionally, this work includes constructing new paved ditches and installing concrete curb and gutter along most of the length of the roadway. This includes installation of several drainage inlets and culverts as well as new striping and signage. The deep subexcavation work includes removal of approximately existing unsuitable material to a 10 feet depth for a continuous 1,000 linear foot length of roadway and replacing with suitable material with geosynthetic reinforcement and installing subsurface drainage. A geotechnical report will be provided with the PS&E package. Reconstructing the existing Buck Hill Overlook parking lot expands and adds more parking spaces and accommodates larger trucks, recreational vehicles, and tour buses. The work includes removing the existing pavement, placing embankment material, new aggregate base, and new hot asphalt concrete pavement. This work also includes constructing accessible parking, placing new concrete sidewalk and curb and gutter, and striping and signage. New trash receptacles and stone benches will be installed as part of the new parking area. Buck Hill Road may be closed for the duration of construction. title: Borough of Millvale, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: This is a Presolicitation Notice only. This is not a Solicitation (Request for Quote). No purchase order will be awarded from this announcement. Any applicable attachments for this project (i.e., Drawings and Specifications) will be issued at the time of the Solicitation. This procurement is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. All interested and capable small business offerors are encouraged to submit a quote. Project Description The Millvale LPP was constructed by U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) in 1980 under the authority of Section 205 of the Flood Control Act of 1948 as amended. The project consists of about 6,200 feet of channel improvement including concrete gravity retaining walls, concrete wall supports, anchored concrete toe blocks, concrete cap walls, stone-filled gabion mattresses, flap gates and access ramps. The LPP is an urban Flood Control Work (FCW), and it is not a multipurpose project. Heavy rains from 1-12 April 2024 caused flooding which damaged the Project within Girty�s Run, including bank erosion, shoaling, erosion of the improved channel, ruptured gabion baskets, washed-out concrete buttresses, and erosion of grouted riprap. Of particular concern are the washed-out buttresses which have migrated to the center of the improved channel, impeding streamflow. If the buttresses are not removed and stream bank improvements continue to deteriorate, there is a risk that debris will continue to accumulate and could ultimately damage the channel downstream of the impediment. To address these damages, Allegheny County requested rehabilitation assistance from USACE through the PL 84-99 program, which authorizes USACE to rehabilitate eligible Federal and non-Federal LPPs damaged or destroyed by floods. An agreement was signed on 6 August 2025 between the Borough of Millvale and USACE to complete the necessary repairs. Some of the major features of work are, but not limited to: Temporary Stream Diversion, Dewatering, and Environmental Controls Stream Flow Control: Design, furnish, operate, maintain, and remove a temporary stream diversion and bypass pumping system to perform all channel bottom and bank work in a dry, dewatered state. Effluent Filtration: Discharge from pumping systems must pass through approved sediment and debris control filtration before re-entering Girty's Run. E&S Controls: Install, inspect, and maintain erosion and sediment controls compliant with PADEP Publication 363-2134-008. The project is located along Girty�s Run and Boomer Run between Station 68+00 and Station 73+80, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $300,000.00 and $350,000.00. The contractor is responsible for all project submittals, including a Quality Control Plan, Accident Prevention Plan, and various shop drawings and product data for government approval. title: Germany – Sanitary fixture installation work – Modernisierung GS Dorschbergschule - Installation von Sanitäreinrichtungen und Installation und Verlegung von Abwasserleitungen
description: Die Grundschule Dorschberg in Wörth a. Rh. wurde 1966 baulich errichtet und liegt hinter dem Mittelbau der Carl–Benz–Gesamtschule in Wörth am Rhein. Die Grundschule besteht aus vier Gebäudeteilen, zu welchen ein ein- bzw. zweigeschossiger Gebäudeteil mit Verbindungsgängen gehört sowie eine Pausenhalle mit einem Verwaltungstrakt und einem eingeschossigen Pavillonbau mit vier Pavillongebäuden. Die Gebäude sind mit Pausengängen verbunden und verfügen über zwei Toilettengebäude. Die ein- bis zweigeschossigen Gebäude wurden in massiver Bauweise mit Beton-Fertigteilen errichtet und weisen Flachdächer in unterschiedlichen Höhenlagen mit umlaufender Attika auf und wurden bis heute mehrfach saniert und modernisiert. Mitte der 1990er Jahre fand eine Betonsanierung statt. In diesem Zuge wurde ein Wärmedämm-Verbundsystem und die Alucobond-Verkleidungen der Attiken und der Fertigteilstützen angebracht. Wesentliche bauliche Maßnahmen - Der bestehende eingeschossige Klassentrakt wird aufgestockt und der bisherige Innenhofbereich zwischen den beiden bestehenden Klassentrakten wird geschlossen und überdacht. Hierzu wird die nicht ausreichend tragfähige Spannbetondecke über dem nördlichen Klassentakt zurück gebaut und durch eine neue Stahlbeton-Massivdecke ersetzt. - Das neue Obergeschoss wird in vorgefertigter Holzbauweise mit tragenden Wänden als Massivholzkonstruktion bzw. Holzständerkonstruktion und oberster Geschossdecke als Brettsperrholzkonstruktion errichtet. - Die zentrale Aula wird mit einer Glasdachkonstruktion versehen. - Die Spannbetondecke im Flurbereich über dem bestehenden Kriechkeller des Nordtraktes muss durch Stahlträger ertüchtigt werden. - Kleinteilige Grundrissänderungen im Bestand - Die Pavillons werden entkernt und zur erweiterten überdachten Pausenhoffläche - Verbesserung des Wärmeschutzes sämtlicher Gebäudehüllflächen (Dachflächen, Fenster, hinterlüftete Holzfassaden, Kellerdeckendämmung) - Modernisierung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung inkl. kontrollierten Lüftungseinrichtung mit Wärmerückgewinnung, energiesparender Beleuchtungssysteme, Gebäudeautomation, einschließlich der digitalen Anforderungen an Schulgebäude - Optimierung des Brandschutzes und Umsetzung des schulischen Schutzkonzepts

title: Germany – Structural shell work – Stadt Drolshagen - Bauliche Erweiterung der Gräfin-Sayn-Verbundgrundschule zum Ausbau der Ganztagsbetreuung am Hauptstandort Drolshagen | Rohbauarbeiten 1. Bauabschnitt
description: Für die Bestandsgebäude der Gräfin-Sayn-Schule in Drolshagen besteht ein baulicher, funktionaler sowie teilweise energetischer Sanierungsbedarf. Zudem ist eine Anpassung an aktuelle pädagogische Anforderungen sowie an moderne Nutzungs- und Raumkonzepte vorgesehen. Im Zuge der geplanten Maßnahmen werden Umbau-, Modernisierungs-, Sanierungs- sowie Teilabbruch- und Erweiterungsmaßnahmen erforderlich. Die Liegenschaftsadresse lautet: Gräfin-Sayn-Schule Am Buscheid 2 57489 Drolshagen Gebäudebeschreibung: Die bestehende Schulanlage der Gräfin-Sayn-Schule besteht aus mehreren miteinander verbundenen bzw. separaten Gebäudeteilen unterschiedlicher Baujahre. Die Gebäude umfassen: • Unterrichts- und Klassenräume • Verwaltungs- und Nebenräume • Sanitärbereiche • Fachräume sowie ergänzende Nutzflächen Die Gebäude sind teilweise mehrgeschossig ausgeführt und über befestigte Schulhofflächen sowie interne Wege miteinander verbunden. Die Außenanlagen bestehen überwiegend aus: • asphaltierten Schulhofflächen • befestigten Zugangs- und Verkehrsflächen • Grün- und Aufenthaltsbereichen Neues Nutzungskonzept: Im Rahmen der geplanten Baumaßnahme wird die bestehende Schulanlage abschnittsweise weiterentwickelt und modernisiert. Die Maßnahmen umfassen insbesondere: • Teilabbruch einzelner Gebäudebereiche, die den heutigen Anforderungen nicht mehr entsprechen • Sanierung und Modernisierung von Bestandsgebäuden, insbesondere im Hinblick auf: • energetische Verbesserung (Dach, Fassade, Fenster) • funktionale Anpassung der Grundrisse • brandschutztechnische Ertüchtigung • Umbauarbeiten im Innenbereich zur Anpassung an das aktuelle Raumprogramm • Ergänzende Neubau- bzw. Erweiterungsmaßnahmen Die Bauausführung erfolgt in mehreren Bauabschnitten, um den Schulbetrieb aufrechtzuerhalten. Die auszuschreibende Leistung betrifft die Rohbauarbeiten für den 1. Bauabschnitt.

description: The Modernization Branch of the F-22 Division (AFLCMC/WAR) is exploring the market for qualified firms to provide next-generation hydrogenated, dielectric cooling fluid. The material shall consist of a synthetic, hydrocarbon base oil with suitable additives as needed. This Sources Sought/RFI is looking for information on improved heat transfer capability. title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded. Q&A will be closed after October 19th. Proposals shall be submitted through the solicitation module in PIEE. See the PIEE submittal instructions for directions on submitting proposal documents in PIEE. Any extensions to this solicitation will be posted here. title: Aircraft Coatings and Sealants OO-ALC
description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, has a need to contract for comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond to this solicitation. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. Contract period of performance dates on the solicitation are estimates and are subject to change according to when the effort gets awarded. Please review and submit any questions related to this solicitation through the PIEE module link found down in the attachments section by October 19th. These questions and answers will be public. QandA will be closed after October 19th. Proposals shall be submitted through the solicitation module in PIEE. See the PIEE submittal instructions for directions on submitting proposal documents in PIEE. Any extensions to this solicitation will be posted here. title: BQM-34S Subsonic Aerial Target (SSAT) Full Rate Production (FRP) Lots 1-4
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Aerial Targets Program Office (PMA-208), located at Patuxent River, MD, intends to negotiate and award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation (NGSC), San Diego, CA. The contemplated action is for the Full Rate Production (FRP) of the BQM-34S Subsonic Aerial Target (SSAT) system, encompassing a base period for FRP Lot 1 and options for FRP Lots 2, 3, and 4. The anticipated production quantity is twenty-five (25) BQM-34S targets per lot, representing a total potential quantity of up to one hundred (100) target systems across all lots. Award is projected for the third quarter (Q3) of Fiscal Year (FY) 2030, with contract deliveries spanning through FY 2036. The BQM-34S SSAT is a recoverable, subsonic aerial target system primarily utilized for naval weapon systems test and evaluation (T&E) and operational Fleet training exercises. This requirement will be procured under the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. NGSC is the sole designer, developer and manufacturer of the BQM-34S SSAT. NGSC is the only known source possessing the requisite knowledge, maintenance and repair experience, and noncommercial technical data and software rights to meet the Government�s requirements for the BQM-34S SSAT System. IMPORTANT ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FOR INTERESTED PARTIES: This synopsis is published for informational purposes only. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which will be considered by the agency. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact NGSC directly via ATTN: AISR&T/RQ-4 or Kelsey Silver at P.O. Box 509066, San Diego, CA 92150-9066. There are no commitments by the Government to issue any solicitations, make an award or awards, or to be responsible for any monies expended by any interested parties before award of a contract for the efforts mentioned above. Information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a contract. No telephone responses will be accepted.
